items.reason: 'Patients with evidence of homozygous (biallelic) RB1 loss by sequencing are excluded from TarGeT-A' restricts entry to the ribociclib strata, and D31-A4 counts an exclusion-stated biomarker as selection (cohort-level, so enrichment). Under corrected D31-A6 it is candidate-matched: CDK4/6 inhibitors such as ribociclib act through RB1, so RB1 loss is the established resistance marker (adjudicator's drug knowledge).

note: Primary outcome is true on the agreed CDK4_6_pathway, CDKN2A_B and PTEN_PI3K rows regardless of the two A-only rows; it is subject to the D21(a) review of positive matches. Priority-3 role difference (eligibility in B vs enrichment in A for the Strata A-D requirement) does not change the outcome; enrichment fits better because Stratum E does not require these alterations. Ribociclib is the only investigational agent in Stratum E (temozolomide backbone), noted by both coders. Paediatric/young adult trial (mixed_age). D31-A4 confirms the RB1-loss exclusion counts as a selection row. A6 resolved (D31-A6 corrected; adjudicator's drug knowledge): TSC1/TSC2 loss activates mTORC1 (everolimus target) and RB1 is required for CDK4/6-inhibitor activity (ribociclib), so both rows are candidate-matched. H3G34 (Stratum E) stays not matched: no established link to ribociclib. XL attention (D31-A2 scope): TarGeT-A entry requires 'at least one relevant actionable somatic alteration' in the cell-cycle OR the PI3K/mTOR pathway, so each row is one route inside an entry criterion and the routes span two pathways, not one; the requirement is kept (every Strata A-D patient enters on an alteration matched to a candidate given to all of them, ribociclib + everolimus), but the primary outcome (true) rests on this judgement.
